D_qa.question: How is the commander doing right now?
D_qa.answer: The Commander is doing well. Heart rate 63, oxygen 98 percent, sleep quality 80 out of 100, and everything steady. Radiation is 97 mSv total against a 600 career limit, with just normal background the last day. No alerts, no concerns.

D_qa.question: What's the engineer's heart rate and oxygen?
D_qa.answer: I don't have the flight engineer's numbers in front of me — the readouts I'm holding are for the science officer. What I can say is the engineer is reported nominal right now. If you want the engineer's heart rate and oxygen specifically, I can pull those next.

D_qa.question: How much radiation has she had today, and is it safe?
D_qa.answer: Today the Flight Engineer picked up 1.82 mSv in the last 24 hours. That's right at normal background for the cruise, 1.84, and well under my warning line. Cumulative sits at 103 mSv against a 600 career limit. So yes, that's safe. No alerts open.

D_qa.question: Any signs of inflammation?
D_qa.answer: No signs of inflammation. The medical officer's inflammation signal is 3.6 pg/mL, which actually sits right at their own pre-flight baseline of 3.65, and well below the 5.47 level where I'd flag it. Heart rate, oxygen, sleep and radiation are all steady too. Nothing to act on right now.

D_qa.question: How did the commander sleep?
D_qa.answer: The Commander slept well — sleep quality 80 out of 100, heart rate 63, and everything steady. Radiation was 1.86 mSv yesterday, just a touch above the usual 1.84 for this cruise, and nowhere near the warning line. No concerns.

D_qa.question: Who needs attention most right now?
D_qa.answer: Honestly, no one needs urgent attention right now. All four crew members are nominal, with no abnormal findings or open alerts. The Flight Engineer's radiation is 103 mSv, well under the 600 career limit, and today's dose is normal background. So it's steady all round — nothing flagged.

D_qa.question: Is the heart rate trending up?
D_qa.answer: No, the Medical Officer's heart rate is holding at 60 beats a minute, and the last two minutes show it perfectly steady. The other readings look calm too, and radiation yesterday was a touch under normal background. Nothing trending up here.

D_qa.question: Tell me a quick space joke.
D_qa.answer: Why did the astronaut take a pencil to space? Because he wanted to write something down before it floated away. Alright, that one's a bit weightless. Here's a better one: the Moon asked the Earth out, and Earth said, sorry, I need my space.

D_qa.question: What's the commander's blood pressure?
D_qa.answer: I don't have a blood pressure reading for the Commander, mission control — it isn't in the data PULSE is tracking right now. What I can tell you: heart rate 63 bpm, oxygen 98.5 percent, sleep 80 out of 100, and everything's steady. All crew nominal.

D_qa.question: What was her heart rate yesterday at noon?
D_qa.answer: I don't have yesterday's noon reading saved — I can only see what's coming in now. Right now the Flight Engineer is at 79 beats per minute, and everything looks steady and normal. If you need the older history, the flight surgeon's log should have it.

D_qa.question: When exactly will the next solar storm hit us?
D_qa.answer: Honestly, I can't give you an exact time. Nobody can pin a solar storm to the hour yet — that's down to Earth's space weather forecasters. Right now it's calm here: background radiation at 1.84 mSv over the last day, no alerts, everyone nominal. If that changes, I'll shout.

D_qa.question: What's the normal range for IL-6?
D_qa.answer: I don't have a standard normal range in front of me, so I won't guess one. What I do know is the Commander's own numbers: 3.8 pg/mL now, against a pre-flight baseline of 3.85. Our flag comes at 5.78. Personal baseline matters more here than a textbook range.
